walkthroughs.body_html:
Grey Matter — a core area of A-Level Biology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Grey Matter brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Grey Matter.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What is the role of the guide RNA in CRISPR-Cas9?
options: Action potentials get bigger as they travel along the axon.
Guide RNA is the new sequence that gets inserted into the genome.
Guide RNA is the enzyme that cuts the DNA.
It directs Cas9 to the specific DNA sequence to cut by base-pairing with the target.

mcqs.q: Why is interspecific competition between similar species important?
options: Competition only happens between predators and their prey.
Action potentials get bigger as they travel along the axon.
Two species cannot occupy exactly the same niche indefinitely — competition often leads to displacement or niche divergence.
Competition means physically fighting and is rare in nature.

mcqs.q: What does the 'all-or-nothing' principle mean for action potentials?
options: Stronger stimuli produce larger action potentials.
Action potentials get bigger as they travel along the axon.
Once threshold is reached, the action potential fires at full size — sub-threshold stimuli produce no action potential.
Guide RNA is the enzyme that cuts the DNA.
